title: Longest Gap Between Consecutive Orders per Customer
description: For each customer, find the **maximum number of days between any two consecutive orders** (the longest gap in their purchase history). Customers with only one order should not appear.
solution_sql: WITH gaps AS (SELECT customer_id, order_date - LAG(order_date) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY order_date) AS gap_days FROM orders) SELECT customer_id, MAX(gap_days) AS max_gap_days FROM gaps WHERE gap_days IS NOT NULL GROUP BY customer_id ORDER BY customer_id

test_cases.description: 4 customers with multiple orders: C1 max gap=26d (Jan15-Feb10), C2 max gap=15d, C3 max gap=54d, C4 max gap=24d. C5 has only one order and is excluded.

hints: Use LAG(order_date) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY order_date) to get the previous order date, then subtract to compute the gap in days.
The first order per customer produces NULL from LAG (no previous order) — filter these out with WHERE gap_days IS NOT NULL before taking MAX.
explanation: LAG fetches the preceding order date within the same customer partition. Subtracting dates gives day gaps. C1: gaps of 14 and 26 days → max=26. C2: gap of 15 days → max=15. C3: gap of 54 days (Jan 10 to Mar 5) → max=54. C4: gaps of 24, 19, 23 → max=24. C5 has one order (NULL from LAG only) → excluded by WHERE. The CTE cleanly separates gap computation from aggregation.
